title: Contractible representable evaluations give the vertical bar augmentation
statement:
Fix the universes of [def-weil-size-convention]. Let $\mathcal D$ be a small ordinary category, $R$ a commutative ring, $F:\mathcal D\to\operatorname{Mod}_R$ a covariant functor, and $Q:\Delta^{\mathrm{op}}\to\mathcal D$ a simplicial object [def-weil-pbc-simplicial-object]. For $p,q\geq0$ put
$$A_{p,q}=\bigoplus_{T_0\to\cdots\to T_p\xrightarrow f Q_q}F(T_0).$$
Horizontal faces delete $T_i$, applying $F(T_0\to T_1)$ when $i=0$ and composing with $f$ when $i=p$; vertical operators postcompose $f$ with the operators of $Q$. Let $\partial_h,\partial_v$ be the alternating face sums in positive respective indices, zero at index zero. Put $A_{p,q}$ in cochain bidegree $(-p,-q)$ and use finite-diagonal total differential $\partial_h+(-1)^p\partial_v$ [def-sp-double-complex-total]. Put $S^{-q}=F(Q_q)$ with alternating-face differential and zero positive terms. Put $B^{-p}=\bigoplus_{T_0\to\cdots\to T_p}F(T_0)$, zero in positive degrees, with alternating faces deleting $T_i$ and applying $F$ only at the first face. Complexes and their derived categories mean [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Assume that for every $T\in\mathcal D$, the simplicial set $\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal D}(T,Q_\bullet)$ admits an inverse to its map to a singleton up to finite zigzags of simplicial cylinder homotopies, that is homotopies $X\times\Delta[1]\to Y$ between the relevant maps [def-weil-pbc-simplicial-set]. For each fixed string $\sigma=(T_0\to\cdots\to T_p)$ put $X_\sigma=\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal D}(T_p,Q_\bullet)$ and $M_\sigma=F(T_0)$. The summation augmentation
$$\bigoplus_{(X_\sigma)_\bullet}M_\sigma\longrightarrow M_\sigma[0]$$
is a chain homotopy equivalence for arbitrary $M_\sigma$, with no flatness hypothesis. Under $R[(X_\sigma)_n]\otimes_R M_\sigma\cong\bigoplus_{(X_\sigma)_n}M_\sigma$, it is the free-chain augmentation tensored with $M_\sigma$. In particular the constant singleton complex, with differential $1$ in positive even degrees and $0$ in odd degrees, has identity section in degree zero and homotopy $h_n=1$ for odd $n$ and $h_n=0$ for even $n$ from section-after-augmentation to the identity. Tensoring its contraction and the chain homotopy equivalence induced by any chosen finite simplicial homotopy zigzags preserves the homotopy identities. Taking direct sums over $\sigma$ gives a chain homotopy equivalence $A_{p,\bullet}\to B^{-p}[0]$ for each $p$. The chain map $e_B:\operatorname{Tot}A\to B$, zero on $q>0$ and forgetting $f$ on $q=0$, is a quasi-isomorphism, hence $e_B:\operatorname{Tot}A\xrightarrow{\sim}B$ in $D(R)$. Both indices are at most zero, so every total diagonal is finite.

proof.text: For a simplicial set $X$, write $C(X)_n=R[X_n]$ with alternating-face differential, zero out of degree zero. The maps $[x]\otimes m\mapsto\iota_x(m)$ give $C(X)_n\otimes_R M\cong\bigoplus_{x\in X_n}M$: the inverse sends a finite-support family $(m_x)$ to $\sum_x[x]\otimes m_x$. These maps commute with every face, since both send the summand indexed by $x$ to that indexed by $d_i x$. Thus, for $X=X_\sigma$ and $M=M_\sigma$, the displayed summation augmentation is exactly the free-chain augmentation tensored with $M$. All indexing sets are small because $\mathcal D$ is small in the fixed universes.

source.place: Tag 08Q9, label lemma-compute-by-cosimplicial-resolution, last paragraph; explicit arbitrary-coefficient identification

proof.text: Fix $\sigma$, put $X=X_\sigma$, and choose the inverse $v:*\to X$ to $u:X\to *$ supplied by the hypothesis. One has $uv=1_*$ strictly. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-simplicial-homotopy-free-chain-homotopy] over $R$ to each cylinder homotopy in the finite zigzag between $vu$ and $1_X$. Reverse a chain homotopy by negation and concatenate by addition. This gives a degree-one map $H$ with $1-C(v)C(u)=dH+Hd$; also $C(u)C(v)=1_{C(*)}$. The cited lemma applies to arbitrary simplicial sets and cylinder homotopies, so no Kan condition or additive inverse on simplicial sets is being assumed.

source.place: Tags 019Y (lemma-functorial-homotopy) and 019S (lemma-homotopy-s-N); finite zigzags as in Tag 019M (remark-homotopy-better)

proof.text: Put $J=C(*)$. Its differential $d_n$ is the alternating sum of $n+1$ identity maps: it is $1$ for positive even $n$ and $0$ for odd $n$. Let $t:J\to R[0]$ and $j:R[0]\to J$ be identity in degree zero and zero otherwise. Put $k_n=1_R:J_n\to J_{n+1}$ for odd $n$ and $k_n=0$ for even $n$. At degree zero, $dk+kd=0=1-jt$; at odd positive degree $d_{n+1}k_n=1$, and at even positive degree $k_{n-1}d_n=1$. Hence $1-jt=dk+kd$ and $tj=1$. Consequently $a=tC(u)$ has inverse $b=C(v)j$: $ab=1$ and $1-ba=d(H+C(v)kC(u))+(H+C(v)kC(u))d$. This proves the free-chain augmentation contraction, including its actual augmentation map.

source.place: Tag 08Q9, last paragraph, singleton comparison; elementary explicit contraction of the unnormalized singleton complex

proof.text: Tensor all the maps and identities in steps 2--3 with $M=M_\sigma$. For example $(dH+Hd)\otimes1=(d\otimes1)(H\otimes1)+(H\otimes1)(d\otimes1)$, so the same $a,b,H+C(v)kC(u)$ tensored with $1_M$ exhibit a chain homotopy equivalence to $M[0]$. This uses additivity and composition of actual linear maps, not exactness of tensor; $M$ is arbitrary. For fixed $p$, choose these data for all strings $\sigma$ and take their direct sums. The differential preserves $\sigma$, and every vector has finite support, so the inverse and homotopy act summandwise and the homotopy identities remain true. The resulting augmentation is $A_{p,\bullet}\to B^{-p}[0]$. It induces isomorphisms on homology: for a cycle $z$, the identity $1-ba=dh+hd$ gives $z-baz=d(hz)$, and $ab=1$ supplies the inverse on classes.

source.place: Tag 08Q9, reduction from direct sums to representable free complexes; explicit tensor and direct-sum homotopy identities

proof.text: Let $L^{i,0}=B^i$ for $i\leq0$, with the bar differential horizontally, and let every other $L^{i,j}$ be zero. The bar face identities follow from composition in $\mathcal D$ and functoriality of $F$; the vertical identities follow from those of $Q$. Horizontal deletion or composition commutes with postcomposition into $Q$, including the last face by associativity and the first by functoriality of $F$. Thus $K^{-p,-q}=A_{p,q}$ is a commuting double complex. Define $e:K\to L$ by forgetting the final arrow at $q=0$ and zero at $q>0$. It commutes with horizontal faces, since forgetting after either composition of the final arrow gives the same string. Vertically the only nonzero check is $q=1$: forgetting $d_0f$ and $d_1f$ gives the same element of $B^{-p}$, so their difference is zero. Hence $e$ is a double-complex map. Its total map is precisely $e_B$, because $(-1)^{-p}=(-1)^p$. In degree $-n$ only $p+q=n$ contributes, giving at most $n+1$ summands; positive total degrees vanish.

source.place: Tag 0132, label lemma-first-quadrant-ss, finite-diagonal setup; direct verification for the displayed bar faces

proof.text: Every column map $e^{i,\bullet}$ is a quasi-isomorphism by step 4 when $i\leq0$, and is the map between zero columns when $i>0$. Both $K$ and $L$ vanish for $i>0$ or $j>0$, and their finite-diagonal totals exist in $\operatorname{Mod}_R$. Apply [lem-pc-bounded-above-double-complex-total-comparison] with $x_0=y_0=0$. Its conclusion is that $\operatorname{Tot}(e)=e_B$ is a quasi-isomorphism. The canonical identification $\operatorname{Tot}(L)=B$ has identity components and the given bar differential, since the vertical differential is zero. By [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], localization at quasi-isomorphisms sends this particular map to an isomorphism $\operatorname{Tot}(A)\xrightarrow{\sim}B$ in $D(R)$. No horizontal compatibility of the chosen column contractions was required: the compared map $e$ itself is compatible by step 5.

lean.statement: theorem contractible_vertical_augmentation (F : D ⥤ ModuleCat.{u} R) (Q : SimplicialObject D) [HasDerivedCategory.{w} (ModuleCat.{u} R)] (hQ : ∀ T : D, ∃ (f : evaluation Q T ⟶ (SimplicialObject.const (Type u)).obj PUnit) (g : (SimplicialObject.const (Type u)).obj PUnit ⟶ evaluation Q T), Relation.EqvGen (fun a b ↦ Nonempty (SSet.Homotopy a b)) (f ≫ g) (𝟙 _) ∧ Relation.EqvGen (fun a b ↦ Nonempty (SSet.Homotopy a b)) (g ≫ f) (𝟙 _)) : Nonempty (Presentation F Q) ∧ (∀ P : Presentation F Q, (∀ p : ℕ, ∃ e : HomotopyEquiv (P.A.X (-↑p)) ((CochainComplex.singleFunctor _ 0).obj (P.B.X (-↑p))), e.hom = P.column p) ∧ QuasiIso P.augmentation ∧ IsIso (DerivedCategory.Q.map P.augmentation)) ∧ (∀ (p : ℕ) (c : ComposableArrows D p) (M : ModuleCat.{u} R), ∃ a : CoefficientAugmentation (evaluation Q c.right) M, (∃ e : HomotopyEquiv ((evaluation Q c.right).chainComplex M) ((ChainComplex.single₀ _).obj M), e.hom = a.augmentation) ∧ (∃ e : HomotopyEquiv ((evaluation Q c.right).chainComplex (ModuleCat.of R R)) ((ChainComplex.single₀ _).obj (ModuleCat.of R R)), e.hom = a.freeAugmentation)) ∧ (∀ M : ModuleCat.{u} R, ∃ (t : ChainComplex.alternatingConst.obj M ⟶ (ChainComplex.single₀ _).obj M) (j : (ChainComplex.single₀ _).obj M ⟶ ChainComplex.alternatingConst.obj M) (k : Homotopy (𝟙 (ChainComplex.alternatingConst.obj M)) (t ≫ j)), t.f 0 = 𝟙 M ∧ j.f 0 = 𝟙 M ∧ j ≫ t = 𝟙 _ ∧ (∀ n : ℕ, k.hom n (n + 1) = if Odd n then 𝟙 M else 0)) ∧ (∀ n : ℤ, Set.Finite {ij : ℤ × ℤ | ij.1 ≤ 0 ∧ ij.2 ≤ 0 ∧ ij.1 + ij.2 = n})
